# LuiUI reusable modules

Local vendored package profile 0.1.0, MIT. These are the canonical sources for the conversation example and collection regression tests; they are reusable independently of the example. Copy this directory into another project's declared Vendor root, declare its files/alias in schema v2, and pin every file's digest in the module lock. Evaluation never downloads dependencies.

- `Scope.New()` owns cleanup, connections and Instances. Dispose is idempotent and runs all cleanup even after a failure. Guards suppress callbacks after retirement.
- `State.New(Initial)` provides Get/Set/Subscribe/Dispose on the existing owner scheduler. Delivery is deterministic, reentrant state writes are coalesced, and subscriptions/delivery passes are bounded. Exceptions become generic framework errors.
- `VirtualList.New(ScrollingFrame, Options)` realizes up to 48 rows from up to 20,000 keyed items. Options provide GetKey, GetHeight and Render; optional MaxRows/Overscan narrow the bounds. Keys must be unique bounded strings and heights finite in [1,4096]. Render initializes a row and owns child connections/Instances through its Scope. It must not recursively update the collection or resize its viewport. Offscreen containers are reused; their old child controls are destroyed and callbacks retired, so an old activation cannot reach a new item. Resident rows preserve stable identity. Invalidate remeasures/rebinds after font/theme changes.

SetItems preserves the first visible stable item and intra-row offset under insert/edit/delete; deleting the anchor preserves/clamps the old logical offset. FollowEnd retains bottom position only when previously at the bottom. Width changes remeasure. There is no automatic scroll/focus into nonresident items; the composer lives outside the collection. Native accessibility exposes resident rows; complete screen-reader navigation of nonresident history remains outside this profile. A viewport needing more than the admitted row count fails explicitly instead of creating an unbounded tree.

Row data remains application-owned. Instances marked sensitive stay classified when containers are reused. Framework errors, collection counters and performance samples never include row keys or text. Model validation precedes replacement; a render failure hides/cleans realized bindings and permits a later refresh to recover.
